24 A vibrating tuning fork is held above a glass cylinder filled to the top with water. The water level is
steadily lowered. A loud sound is first heard when the water level is 83.5 cm above the bench.
The next loud sound is heard when the water level is 17.1 cm above the bench.
tuning fork
NOT TO
SCALE

water

The speed of sound in air is 340 m s–1.
What is the frequency of the tuning fork?
A
128 Hz

hints: Notice the air column gets longer as water is lowered, so find the change in air length from $83.5\text{ cm} - 17.1\text{ cm}$.
Recall that the air column with water at the bottom is closed at one end, so successive loud resonances occur when the length increases by $\lambda/2$.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and your value of $\lambda$ from half-wavelength $= 66.4\text{ cm}$ to find $f$.
walkthrough: The tube is closed by water at the bottom and open at the top, so each loud sound is a stationary-wave resonance.
As water is lowered the air length increases. The increase equals the fall in water level: $\Delta L = 83.5\text{ cm} - 17.1\text{ cm} = 66.4\text{ cm} = 0.664\text{ m}$.
For a closed pipe, successive resonances are $\lambda/2$ apart in length, so $\lambda/2 = 0.664\text{ m}$.
With $v = f\lambda$, $f = v/\lambda = 340/1.328 \approx 256\text{ Hz}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Gives half the correct frequency, from misusing the $66.4\text{ cm}$ separation as $\lambda$ with an extra factor of 2.

B.explanation: The $66.4\text{ cm}$ increase in air column equals $\lambda/2$, giving $\lambda = 1.328\text{ m}$ and $f = 340/1.328 \approx 256\text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Too large by a factor of 1.5, not obtained from $v = f\lambda$ with $\lambda/2 = 83.5-17.1\text{ cm}$.

D.explanation: Double the correct frequency, from taking the $66.4\text{ cm}$ separation as one full wavelength $\lambda$.
